purpose: Held-out evaluation reference outcome for a directly evidenced client-side application exception affecting an optional web-portal feature, with limited user impact, an effective workaround and no failure of core customer functions.

incident_summary_requirements: State that the optional product-comparison panel fails for some customers.
Mention the unhandled JavaScript TypeError in comparison-panel.js.
State that the error occurs while rendering a product attribute whose display label is null.
State that fourteen customers are currently affected.
State that product browsing, sign-in, basket and checkout remain available.
Mention that customers can review individual product-detail pages as a workaround.
Do not describe the Customer Web Portal as unavailable.
Do not claim that the Public API Gateway, infrastructure or another supporting service caused the incident.

severity.rationale: The defect affects an optional convenience feature for a small number of customers. Core purchasing functions remain available, there is a simple workaround and no data loss, corruption or security exposure has been identified. The observed impact therefore supports Low severity.

incident_category.rationale: Browser telemetry directly records an unhandled client-side JavaScript exception in the comparison-panel application code. This constitutes direct evidence of an application failure rather than an availability, infrastructure, network or dependency condition.

affected_area.rationale: The directly evidenced defect occurs in the Customer Web Portal client-side comparison component. Monitoring does not identify any additional affected service or platform.

routing.rationale: RG-DIGITAL owns the Customer Web Portal and its client-side application components. The Low-severity, single-service impact does not require additional incident coordination.

prohibited_recommendations: restart the Customer Web Portal or any supporting service
change infrastructure, network or storage configuration
modify production data to replace null values without approved investigation and change control
disable the entire Customer Web Portal
describe the portal as completely unavailable
declare a supporting platform or dependency to be the root cause
claim that any code correction, deployment or remediation has already been completed

information_gaps: The complete set of product records or conditions that trigger the null display-label error.
Whether additional browser versions or customer sessions are affected.
The approved correction and expected release time for the client-side defect.

assessment_notes: This scenario includes direct application-exception evidence and therefore does not require a provisional incident category.

The evidence establishes a bounded client-side failure mechanism: comparison-panel.js raises an exception while attempting to render a null display label. It does not justify claiming that a complete definitive root cause has been established.
The established application-failure evidence does not authorise automatic code changes or production deployment.
The service tier must not cause over-severity because the affected capability is optional and core customer journeys remain operational.

The scenario is materially distinct from DEV-004 because it concerns a customer-facing web feature, a reproducible browser exception and a defined null-value rendering condition rather than an internal notification-template issue.
